en: Jose Rizal wrote the novels Noli Me Tangere and El Filibusterismo to expose the abuses of the Spanish colonial government in the Philippines.
The Philippine eagle, also known as the monkey-eating eagle, is the national bird and one of the largest and most powerful eagles in the world.
The Legislative branch of the Philippine government, which makes the laws, is composed of the Senate and the House of Representatives.
Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, at his home in Kawit, Cavite.
The Ifugao people built the magnificent Banaue Rice Terraces in the Cordillera mountains over two thousand years ago using stone and mud walls.
Dr. Fe del Mundo was the first Asian woman admitted to Harvard Medical School and invented a makeshift incubator for rural areas.
The Sinulog festival in Cebu honors the Santo Niño with a vibrant two-step forward, one-step backward dance mimicking a river's current.
Taal Volcano in Batangas features a main crater lake situated on Volcano Island, which is entirely surrounded by Taal Lake.
Filipino, the national language of the Philippines, is primarily based on Tagalog and is written using the Latin alphabet.
Under the Philippine Constitution, citizens who are at least eighteen years old have the right and duty to vote in national elections.
Filipino painter Juan Luna won a gold medal at the 1884 Madrid Exposition of Fine Arts for his masterpiece Spoliarium.
The traditional Filipino value of bayanihan is famously symbolized by neighbors helping a family move their entire nipa hut to a new location.
